# Sparse and Efficient Representations

Also called: Sparse NeRF, KiloNeRF, Mega-NeRF, SRF, ProNeRF, NeRF-XL

## Overview
Sparse and Efficient Representations address the computational and memory bottlenecks of dense, global Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) by decomposing the scene representation into localized, sparse, or structured components. This family enables scalable training and rendering for large-scale scenes or high-resolution details that would otherwise exceed hardware limits. Unlike global implicit models, these methods partition the scene spatially or structurally, allowing for parallel optimization, reduced query complexity, or adaptive sampling. Key distinctions among siblings include: [Mega-NeRF Spatial Partitioning](8776-mega-nerf-spatial-partitioning.md) uses a 2D grid of independent MLPs for large-scale fly-throughs; [Sparse Radiance Field (SRF) Representation](8876-sparse-radiance-field-srf-representation.md) employs a sparse 3D voxel grid for direct differentiable rendering; [KiloNeRF](8942-kilonerf.md) distills a global teacher into thousands of tiny student MLPs; [ProNeRF](9673-pronerf.md) uses projection-aware sampling to reduce sample counts; and [NeRF-XL Multi-GPU Representation Strategy](#nerf-xl-multi-gpu-representation-strategy) distributes parameters across GPUs for capacity scaling.

## Shared principles
The core principle of this family is the decomposition of the scene representation to improve efficiency. While specific implementations vary, they share the goal of reducing the computational load per query or the total memory footprint compared to a single monolithic NeRF. This is achieved through:
1.  **Spatial Partitioning:** Dividing the scene into regions (cells, voxels, tiles) handled by separate sub-networks or data structures [S1].
2.  **Sparsity:** Storing features only for occupied regions, ignoring empty space [S1].
3.  **Localization:** Using local information (e.g., nearest centroid, nearby reference views) to predict radiance, reducing the need for global context in every query [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Mega-NeRF Spatial Partitioning](8776-mega-nerf-spatial-partitioning.md)
Decomposes large-scale scenes into a 2D grid of spatial cells, each managed by a lightweight MLP submodule. It is chosen for large-scale virtual fly-throughs where global models are intractable. It differs from KiloNeRF by using a fixed 2D grid with fixed height and independent optimization per cell, rather than a 3D grid with distillation.

### [Sparse Radiance Field (SRF) Representation](8876-sparse-radiance-field-srf-representation.md)
A voxel-based representation storing density and radiance in a sparse 3D grid (COO format). It serves as a direct, differentiable alternative to MLPs. It is chosen when fast volume rendering and mesh extraction (via Marching Cubes) are required. It differs from Mega-NeRF by using explicit voxel storage rather than MLP submodules.

### [KiloNeRF](8942-kilonerf.md)
Decomposes a large NeRF into a set of small, shallow MLPs arranged in a 3D grid, trained via teacher-student distillation. It is chosen for accelerating rendering by up to three orders of magnitude. It differs from Mega-NeRF by using a 3D grid and distillation from a global teacher, rather than independent training on partitioned data.

### [ProNeRF](9673-pronerf.md)
A sampler-based method using a Projection-Aware Sampling (PAS) network to predict sampling points and opacity adjustments. It is chosen for achieving a superior speed-quality trade-off (15–23× faster) with fewer samples. It differs from the others by focusing on adaptive sampling guided by reference view projections rather than spatial partitioning of the model itself.

### NeRF-XL Multi-GPU Representation Strategy
A parameter distribution strategy for multi-GPU NeRF training where each GPU handles a distinct 3D tiled region with independent hash encoding and density MLP, but shares the color MLP and appearance/camera embeddings across all GPUs [S1]. Unlike independent training where each GPU has its own full NeRF, this method unifies instantiations as a 'single NeRF' with spatially partitioned parameters, increasing model capacity without redundancy [S1]. Hash Encoding and Density MLPs are independent per GPU, confined within a non-overlapping bounding box [S1]. The Color MLP is shared across all GPUs using Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) to ensure consistent color prediction for novel views [S1]. Appearance Embeddings are shared across GPUs; set to zero during novel-view rendering if enabled during training [S1]. Camera Pose Embeddings are shared across GPUs if camera optimization is enabled [S1].

## Background
The need for sparse and efficient representations arose from the limitations of standard NeRFs in handling large-scale scenes and high-resolution details. Mega-NeRF was introduced to enable large-scale virtual fly-throughs [S1]. Sparse Radiance Fields (SRF) and KiloNeRF were developed to accelerate rendering and reduce memory overhead by leveraging sparsity and decomposition [S1]. ProNeRF was proposed to improve the speed-quality trade-off through adaptive sampling [S1]. NeRF-XL was introduced to scale NeRFs using multiple GPUs by distributing parameters [S1].
